enumeration_note: One opening-range-breakout skeleton taught two ways with different entry triggers, so split into two objects (per the retest-vs-breakout distinction): (0) the breakout entry (enter on the break of the OR high/low; grouped 5/15/30-minute timeframe variants) and (1) the pullback entry (enter on a pullback to the pullback level after the break). This is a conceptual onboarding (video 1); the pullback is a named taught setup with a precisely defined entry level but its exit is only gestured via the shared half/full-range target framework.

coaching_notes: Understanding the psychology of these breakouts really can help you transform your trading (the range high is where sellers stepped in with conviction; the range low is where buyers defended with strength).
The opening range acts as a decision point for the rest of the day, relative to that particular day's volatility.

ENTRY: long on breakout above the opening range high; short on breakout below the opening range low; direction follows whichever side breaks
STOP: half range stop = a half-range distance beyond the opening range level
TARGET: half range target = opening range level + (range value Ã· 2)
